sources.name: Swift J1727.8−1613
sources.notes: Hard-state jet and detached Knot 0. The peak hard-state Eddington ratio is not specific to the radio imaging epoch. Distance follows Burridge et al. (2025).
sources.calibration: Original Wood et al. Fig. 2. 10 mas = 154 native pixels; 5.5 kpc. The 40° inclination and 10-solar-mass black hole are adopted.

sources.name: Cygnus X-1
sources.notes: Six-epoch 2016 VLBA stack showing both jet and counterjet. The inclination is adopted from the binary orbit; Prabu et al. constrain a small jet–orbit misalignment.
sources.calibration: Released BM429Stack.fits; 0.0500000008 mas per native pixel, no added smoothing. Logarithmic display above 5σ (~0.05 mJy/beam). Radio brightness peak is the approximate origin.

sources.name: 1E 1740.7−2942
sources.notes: The “Great Annihilator”, the original microquasar discovered by Mirabel et al. (1992). The image is the April 1992 epoch reprocessed by Luque-Escamilla et al. (2015), showing the arcminute-scale jet/lobe structure. Mass and distance are adopted comparison values, not dynamical measurements. The jet inclination is uncertain, so its size stays projected in both modes. The northern lobe is rotated downward.
sources.calibration: Luque-Escamilla et al. (2015), Fig. 2, left 1992 panel. Declination ticks: 15 arcsec = 123 embedded-raster pixels; native angular pixel size 0.121951 arcsec. At the adopted 8.5 kpc this is 0.0050255 pc/pixel. Nucleus is the central radio-contour peak, within ~4 pixels of the quoted position. Only the jet contour aperture is retained; axes, beam and separated noise islands are removed. The 2015 paper discusses a model-dependent ~5-kpc distance alternative. Approximate Eddington ratio is representative of later hard-state measurements, not simultaneous with the 1992 radio image.

sources.name: GRS 1758−258
sources.notes: MeerKAT image of the parsec-scale jet/ISM interaction lobes and radio core. The northern lobe is oriented downward for comparison. Mariani et al. quote deprojected core-to-lobe distances of 3.36 pc north and 4.41 pc south (about 7.8 pc end to end). The adopted 61° comes from X-ray disc reflection and assumes disc–jet alignment. The 10-solar-mass black hole is assumed, not dynamically measured. The Eddington range characterises representative hard-state X-ray observations, not the lobe-averaged power or a simultaneous 2024 measurement. Colours and source apertures are illustrative.
sources.calibration: Original Mariani et al. (2025), Fig. 1b embedded map, 1791 × 2048 pixels. Declination ticks 30 arcsec ≈ 304.23 pixels; independently calibrated RA agrees to 0.08%. Projected scale 0.0986101 arcsec/pixel = 0.00406364 pc/pixel at 8.5 kpc. Core from RA 18h01m12.400s, Dec −25°44′36.10″. Source apertures guided by Fig. 2 omit unrelated field sources. Rotated 172° counterclockwise, no geometric stretching. Projected R_G calibration uses 10 M☉; optional 61° deprojection is applied once.

sources.name: NGC 6251 (jet)
sources.notes: Extended radio jet extracted from the published montage. Its printed 100-kpc bar sets an approximate historical length calibration; the original distance convention has not been independently recovered.
sources.calibration: Printed 100 kpc = 270 native pixels. Adopted M = 6 × 10⁸ M☉ and i = 30°. Approximate scale inherited from the vetted montage.

sources.name: NGC 6251 (lobes)
sources.notes: NGC 6251: full LOFAR view of the jet, both outer lobes and the faint northern extension. This is a separate, much larger component from the VLA jet entry. The outer structures retain their projected dimensions; the inner jet’s adopted 30° angle is not applied to them. The lobes integrate past activity over hundreds of millions of years.
sources.calibration: Cantwell et al. (2020), Fig. 2; source aperture guided by their Fig. 7 masks unrelated field sources. Approximate isotropic TAN calibration fitted to the RA/Dec ticks, using the paper’s 0.498 kpc/arcsec; 3.260 kpc per rendered pixel (~1% scale precision). Core from the catalogued nucleus, accurate to approximately 3 rendered pixels. The full bent LOFAR extent is not forced to the historical 1.7-Mpc span.

references.label: Cantwell et al. (2020) · full LOFAR source

sources.name: Centaurus A (inner lobes)
sources.notes: Both inner radio lobes are shown. The northern inner lobe is oriented downward for comparison. This is not the much larger outer-lobe system.
sources.calibration: Burns et al. Fig. 1 upper map; 2-arcmin bar = 72 native pixels. Recalibrated to 3.8 Mpc. Adopted i = 50°.

sources.name: Centaurus A (outer lobes)
sources.notes: Full giant-lobe system from the MWA image publicised by ICRAR. About 0.5 Mpc across in projection. Some compact background radio sources remain superposed inside the lobe aperture. The inner-jet angle is not applied to the outer lobes; the Eddington ratio describes the present nucleus.
sources.calibration: Calibrated directly to McKinley et al. (2022), Fig. 1: original declination ticks 2° = 202 pixels at 180-dpi page rendering. Registration using 71 compact-source peaks gives 178.77 pixels per 2° in the resized publicity image; at 3.8 Mpc, about 742 pc per asset pixel. Core located from the sky-coordinate grid. Rotated 6° counterclockwise; no outer-lobe deprojection. Supersedes the initial 2025-reproduction bar calibration (length correction +13.5%).

sources.name: M87
sources.notes: Full outer radio halo, retained in projection. The inner jet inclination does not establish a single viewing angle for the outer lobes. The radio nucleus is located approximately (±15 native pixels).
sources.calibration: Owen et al. Fig. 1 original embedded raster: 20 projected kpc = 419 native pixels. Outer-halo morphology is rotated vertically; no inclination correction.

sources.name: Alcyoneus
sources.notes: Low-excitation, radiatively inefficient radio galaxy with a published projected extent of 4.99 ± 0.04 Mpc. The mass is inferred from the stellar velocity dispersion, not directly measured dynamically. The full jet and lobe image is retained projected: the two lobes have different modelled orientations. The Eddington ratio is a qualitative jet-mode inference, not a measured nuclear bolometric luminosity.
sources.calibration: Oei et al. (2022), Fig. 1 original embedded 2048 × 2048 image. Its caption specifies a 2048-arcsec square field centred on the host, giving 1 arcsec per native pixel. At the paper’s 4.0 kpc/arcsec this is 4000 projected pc/pixel. Orange LOFAR emission is isolated from the blue WISE background, with the two lobes and central jets retained and recoloured silver. Native core (1023.5, 1023.5), approximate to 3 pixels; rotate 127° clockwise. Lobes have 60-arcsec resolution and jets 6-arcsec resolution. The quoted 4.99-Mpc measurement comes from the paper’s separate compact-source-subtracted 90-arcsec image; the colour-image envelope is not forced to that exact length.
